A NEW EXPLORER STUMBLES UPON THE FORGOTTEN PATH, READY TO FEED THE HUNGRY
Searching for their missing child, fueled by concern and parental rage, a new explorer ventures underground.
A temporal anomaly in The Facility thrusts the janitor into the biggest cleanup of their career.
When she breaks in to rescue the animals, the activist stumbles into a fungal hell.
Armed with their trusty tools, the Machinist delves into the rusted remains of The Facility.
Fatten up your foes to help you roast a bounty of the most delicious toasties possible!
Always searching, harness the power of your emotions to help you do whatever it takes to find what went missing.
Trash is no problem! Gunk is your friend! Let's clean up this mess!
Venture deeper to liberate the creatures of The Facility, and call on their aid when you need them the most!

One wrong turn off my route and the streets just... stopped. So I'm doing what I always do - keep moving, keep my distance, and let the papers fly. Somebody down here has to be expecting a delivery.

Thirty years behind that counter and not so much as a <i>thank you<i/> - so I hung up my hairnet and walked, and kept walking till the halls turned to tunnels. Ladle's still in my hand, slop's still hot, and this lot lined up looks hungry. A line's a line. Nobody leaves my counter empty handed.

My kid never came home from the paper route. No one else was going to go looking, so I followed the trail down here myself - no weapon, no plan, just a parent who's not turning back without them. Hang on, sweetheart. I'm coming.

The work order came in with no name on it - just an address that led down and down and never quite stopped. So I grabbed my cart and followed it, because that's the job. Big mess waiting at the bottom. Might as well start scrubbing.

I heard what they were doing to the animals in that place, so I climbed the fence and let myself in - no permission, no backup, nobody the wiser. The cages went deeper than I thought. They feel pain just like us, and I'm not leaving a single one behind.

Nobody remembers the person who fixes things. They remember the person who cuts the ribbon. Well, the ribbon-cutters are long gone, and here I am, drawn back down into the rust. Give me a busted machine and five minutes; I'll make it better than it ever was.
Rest for the night.\nBeware of creeping danger.

Oh, spilled already? I hadn't even leaned in.
You came apart before you were worth the swallow.
A crumb. Not even a mouthful.
Three steps, and all your juice on the floor.
Picked green off the vine. And I do love you sweet.
Thin. You'd have thickened, given a season.
You again. Same green flavour as before.
Mm. I can smell you softening.
That looked tender. I felt it from here.
Warm and dark now. Settle into me.
Ohh, you've gone soft right through the middle.
All of you, let out at once. Such a waste of good stock.
Hush. Nothing gnaws at you in here but me.
Down you go, into the dark of me.
So close, the warmth of you reached my lips.
One tunnel more and I'd have had a sip.
Sweetened the whole way down, and spoiled on my very step.
I had my mouth open for you.
There you are. Sweet, and right on time.
All the way down, and still warm. Come in, come in.
At last. Let me chew those bright hard edges of yours.
Perfect. Perfectly done. Hold still now.
You'll come back sweeter. Your kind always do.
Still so green. Still so raw.
Barely a taste. You've left me wanting.
You gave at the world's very first bite.
I'd hoped for a little more meat on you.
You're not ready to be swallowed. Not nearly.
Your flavour will hang in the spore for the next.
Perhaps the next crawler comes riper.
I thought you might've been ready for me.
Plump enough, but you burst too early.
A single breath from my lips, you were.
The greycaps supped you before I could.
I could smell you. I could almost chew.
Your warmth got here before the rest of you did.
Down to the very bottom of me.
You made yourself sweet and walked right in. Good.
Back in the soft dark of me, where you're kept.
Every warm inch of you. Mine now.
One morsel nearer the bright world above.
I bloom a little wider, with you inside me.
Perfectly ripe. Perfectly done... though the ripe ones sometimes turn my stomach.
Not yet sweet enough to keep down.
Underdone. Back on the vine with you.
Only the sweet ones reach my table.
How many steps before you split?
Shall I show you how much of you went uneaten?
Let's see how far you softened.
How far down the wormholes did you crawl?
How many tunnels, before the gunk had you?
Wondering how near my mouth you came?
How close to the swallow were you?
Look how nearly you fed me.
You spoiled right here, on my lip.
See how well you ripened for me.
This is what a finished plate looks like.
For feeding me, a little of your taste is kept back.
Only the one flavour left to leave. Go on.
Leave a taste in the spore, for the next to follow your trail.
Done. The spore holds it now.
Only the ones who crawl all the way to me get to leave a taste behind.
May it season the ones who crawl after you.
Not the flavour I'd have left. But it's yours.
Another little morsel for the road.
If that's the taste you'd leave behind...
